process.title: How a search runs
process.note: US searches typically run six to ten weeks from the intake call to a signed offer, and US notice periods are short, so the start date follows quickly. German searches run longer and are governed by notice periods — see how the two markets differ.

method.title: How I measure this
method.intro: A number without a definition is marketing. Here is exactly what each figure counts, and what it leaves out.

items.definition: Business days from signed engagement to delivery of the first shortlist of three or more qualified candidates.
items.excludes: Client-side delays longer than three business days, and searches rescoped after kickoff.

items.definition: Calendar days from signed engagement to written offer acceptance. This is not the start date — in the US that normally follows two to four weeks later, after notice.
items.excludes: Searches cancelled, frozen, or materially rescoped mid-process, and offers withdrawn by the client.

items.definition: Placed candidates still employed by the client, or promoted within it, twelve months after their first day, divided by the placements old enough to have reached twelve months.
items.excludes: Layoffs, restructures, role eliminations and site closures — departures the candidate did not choose and I could not have predicted.

items.definition: If a placement leaves or is terminated within 90 days of starting, I run the search again at no additional fee. The clock starts on the candidate's first day, and the guarantee is written into the engagement agreement before the search begins.
items.excludes: Nothing is excluded by role elimination or a change of plan on your side — if you no longer need the role, you owe me nothing further.

method.window: Figures cover placements since 2015 and are reviewed each quarter. If you want the underlying counts before you sign anything, ask me on the first call and I will send them.
method.benchmarkNote: For context: SHRM's 2026 benchmark puts median US time-to-fill at 39 days across non-executive roles, and published benchmarks for industrial and manufacturing sales run 45 to 75 days. A specialist working one market with a live network should beat that, and this is by how much.

markets.title: A US search and a German search do not run the same way
markets.intro: If you report into a German parent, this is the difference you will spend the most time explaining to them. It is worth knowing before you set a start date.

markets.note: German federal statistics put the average time a reported vacancy stays open at around 95 days for roles requiring a degree and about 140 days for skilled trades. Neither number includes the notice period that follows.

industries.title: The industries I work in
industries.subtitle: What I actually screen for
industries.intro: I recruit commercial and technical people for industrial manufacturers. These are the four areas I work, the roles inside them, and the questions I use to tell a credible candidate from a plausible one.

sectors.name: Industrial automation and sensor technologies
sectors.roles: Sales engineers, application engineers, regional sales managers
sectors.tech: Sensing, industrial connectivity, safety and control components, PLCs and I/O, control architecture, robotics, factory automation
sectors.channel: OEM and end-user accounts, run alongside distribution
sectors.screen: Can they walk a production floor, work out why the sensing is failing, and close the fix? Do they know where sensing sits in a control architecture well enough to hold that conversation with a controls engineer?

sectors.name: Motion control and drives
sectors.roles: District and territory sales, OEM account management, channel management
sectors.tech: Gear motors, variable-frequency drives, motion control systems, power transmission; sizing from torque, speed, duty cycle and ambient conditions
sectors.channel: Direct OEM and stocking distributors at the same time, which need different handling
sectors.screen: Can they size a gearbox from an application sheet and defend the math? Have they genuinely run direct and distribution in parallel, or only one of the two?

sectors.name: Process instrumentation and valve automation
sectors.roles: Account managers and sales engineers into refining, petrochemical and midstream
sectors.tech: Control valves, isolation valves, flow measurement, actuation and materials selection; how DCS, PLC and SCADA relate to the instrumentation
sectors.channel: Project and MRO in parallel, EPC bid packages, turnaround and outage support
sectors.screen: Have they walked a unit during a turnaround? Do they know which EPC writes the spec and which one forwards the package?

sectors.name: Test and measurement
sectors.roles: Sales and commercial leadership, business unit management
sectors.tech: Electrical test equipment, cable fault location, pipeline leak detection, bulk and process measurement
sectors.channel: Direct and subsidiary sales organizations across Europe and the US
sectors.screen: This is where my longest client relationships sit, including Megger since 2016. The reference letters on the references page come from this sector.

industries.note: If your product line sits next to one of these rather than inside it, say so on the first call. I would rather tell you it is not my patch than learn it in week six.

items.a: A percentage of first-year total compensation, agreed in writing before I start. You get the number on the first call. That call is free and nothing follows from it automatically.

items.q: What happens if the hire does not work out?
items.a: A written 90-day replacement guarantee: if the person leaves or is let go within 90 days of their first day, I run the search again at no additional fee. Ninety days is the US standard — around 85% of agency guarantees fall in the 30-to-90-day band, and most are replacement-only rather than a refund. The clock starts on the candidate's first day, and it is in the engagement agreement before the search begins.

Usually, and the search is better for it. I will not spend eight weeks mapping a market in order to race three other agencies to the same five people. If exclusivity is a problem, say so and we will talk it through.

items.q: Can you really recruit in the US from Germany?
items.a: Yes. US searches run by phone and video, and I work your morning. If someone needs to be met in person, I say so and we plan for it.

I have recruited for measurement, test and instrumentation manufacturers since 2015. I will not pretend to know your product line better than you do. After the intake call I will know enough to hold a credible conversation with an engineer who does.
I do. There is no research team, no account manager, and nobody hands you off after the sale. That is the trade: one experienced person rather than a bench.

items.q: How fast will I see candidates?
items.a: For a US search, a shortlist of three or more inside five business days of a signed engagement, and typically about twenty days to a written offer acceptance. For a German or Swiss search, expect a shortlist in three to four weeks and a start date three to six months out, because notice periods there run to the end of a quarter.

items.q: Where do you find people, if not job boards?
items.a: I map the companies where the right background actually sits — your competitors, adjacent product categories, the distribution channel — and approach those people directly, mostly through LinkedIn Recruiter and the phone. Almost nobody I place was looking when I called.
No. Staffing agencies place contractors and temporary workers at volume and bill hourly. I run individual permanent searches, one at a time, and I am paid once on a successful hire.

items.q: How do you judge whether a technical candidate is credible?
items.a: I ask them to do the work in conversation. Size the gearbox from the application sheet. Explain why the sensing is failing on that line. Tell me which EPC writes the spec. People who have done the job answer immediately, and people who have been near it do not.

One call, forty-five minutes, no charge. We go through the role, the territory, the compensation band and what a good first year looks like. You get the fee and the guarantee in writing after that call, and nothing happens until you sign it.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: Philipp Hoffschröer, Founder
about.description: I'm Philipp Hoffschröer. I have recruited technical sales and engineering people since 2015 — part-time at first, alongside operating roles at two software companies, and full-time on it now. I work mainly with manufacturers of measuring and test equipment.

body.market: Most of my clients are German manufacturers with U.S. operations, or U.S. subsidiaries reporting into a German parent. That is a specific hiring problem. The role needs someone who can hold a technical conversation with a plant engineer in Ohio and a product conversation with a development team in Baden-Württemberg, who understands how a German parent makes decisions, and who will still be in the seat in three years. The people who can do that are employed, and they are not on job boards.
body.placed: What I have placed: sales engineers and application engineers, regional and national sales managers, business unit heads, and site management. Megger Germany has hired through me repeatedly since 2016 — their managing director's signed reference letter is on the references page.
body.reach: I am based in Germany and work U.S. hours through midday Eastern. Email is the fastest way to reach me, and it reaches me, not an assistant.
body.numbers: Of the candidates I have placed, 92% are still with the client twelve months later, or have been promoted inside it. How I count that is set out below.

direct.title: I go find people
direct.description: Most of the people I place were not looking. I map the companies where the right background sits, approach people directly, and work references. I don't post an ad and wait to see what arrives.

documented.title: You see the downside too
documented.description: Every profile I send says where the candidate is weak, not only where they are strong: compensation gaps, relocation reluctance, where they will need support in the first year.

honest.title: I tell you when it won't work
honest.description: If the band is below market, the timeline is unrealistic, or the role isn't placeable as written, you hear it on the first call — not after six months of invoices.

discretion.title: Nobody's name moves without permission
discretion.description: Your search stays confidential. No candidate's name reaches you until they have agreed to it, and you see an anonymized summary first.

about.background: Three years at KPMG in finance advisory, then commercial roles at Lufthansa and Deichmann. Co-Founder and Chief Business Development Officer at emteria GmbH, and CEO Germany at Studo.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Skytz Consulting is a trade name of Laurasia LLC ("we", "us", "our"). This policy explains what personal information we collect, why, and what you can ask us to do about it. It covers U.S. state privacy laws including the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA), and the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) for visitors in Europe.

usRights.title: 4. Your rights in the United States
usRights.description: We do not sell or share personal information, and we do not process it for cross-context behavioral advertising. California residents have the right to know what personal information we collect, to request a copy, to request correction or deletion, and to be free from retaliation for exercising those rights. Residents of other U.S. states with comparable privacy laws have equivalent rights. To exercise any of them, email us using the address in section 11 — we will verify your identity and respond within the period your state's law requires.

legalBasis.title: 5. If you are in Europe (GDPR)
legalBasis.intro: For individuals in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland, we process personal data on the following legal bases:

items.consent: Consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR): where you have given explicit consent for specific processing
items.contract: Contractual necessity (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR): where processing is necessary to perform a contract or take pre-contractual steps
items.legitimate: Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR): where processing is necessary for our legitimate business interests, such as direct outreach, fraud prevention, and service improvement
items.legal: Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR): where processing is required by applicable law

legalBasis.rights: You also have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, data portability, objection, withdrawal of consent, and the right to complain to a supervisory authority.

sharing.title: 6. Who we share it with
sharing.description: We do not sell personal information. We may share it with: (a) clients, solely for recruiting purposes and only with your consent; (b) service providers who support our operations under confidentiality agreements; (c) authorities where required by law. Data may be transferred to the United States, where Laurasia LLC is registered. Transfers from Europe are made under Standard Contractual Clauses where applicable.

retention.title: 7. How long we keep it
retention.description: We keep personal information only as long as necessary: (a) client and candidate data for the duration of the business relationship plus 6 years for legal compliance; (b) website usage data for up to 26 months; (c) communication records for 3 years after last contact. You can ask us to delete it earlier, subject to legal retention requirements.

security.title: 8. Security
security.description: We use appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal information against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction, including encryption and access controls.
